species.name: Clocklet

dex.text: A sunny little bud among toothed leaves, up at dawn and shut by dusk. It grows in the cracks in a pavement and rather enjoys it.
dex.fact: Dandelion flowers open in the morning and close at night and in dull weather.

species.real: The name dandelion comes from the French dent de lion, meaning lion's tooth, after the jagged leaves.

species.name: Dandylion

dex.text: A golden mane, a leafy tail and a loud opinion of every lawn in the parish. It is not a flower you can easily pull up.
dex.fact: A dandelion has a long taproot, which is why digging one out and leaving a scrap behind just means another one grows.

species.real: The yellow dandelion head is not one flower but a cluster of many tiny flowers, called florets.

species.name: Clockmaster

dex.text: A white puff with a clock face in it, correct twice a day and whenever you do not need it. Blow on it and it will tell you the time, with feeling.
dex.fact: Each seed of a dandelion clock has a tiny parachute of hairs, and the wind can carry it many miles.

species.real: Children have blown on dandelion clocks to tell the time for generations, counting the puffs it takes to blow all the seeds away.
